lessons.title: Replying to an email with AI
lessons.subtitle: One complaint, one draft, one check

sections.title: The Bergmann complaint
sections.content:
Bergmann is angry. The regular customer orders hydraulic components, the last delivery came eight working days late, and Procurement wants two things: an explanation, and corrective action that holds.

Has your organization approved an assistance function for exactly this purpose? Then let it write a draft. What the interface looks like depends on product and version. The instruction runs like this:

"Draft a response to the complaint. Use only the facts below. Tone: respectful and factual. Maximum 150 words. Do not invent a cause, deadline, compensation, or corrective action. Mark missing information in square brackets."

Into the prompt goes only what the purpose needs and the approved workflow covers. Redaction and pseudonymization lower the risk. An unapproved service they do not make permissible.

No approved system? Then you write the draft yourself, or practise on a fully synthetic example. The real customer mail does not travel into some consumer offer.
sections.keyTakeaway: The assistant delivers a draft, no more. Supported facts in, gaps marked, and only inside the approved workflow.

sections.title: Five questions before you send
sections.content:
The draft is there. Read it like any business text you would sign:

1. **Facts and source:** Do the order, delay, and prior correspondence match the primary records?
2. **Authority:** Does the draft contain deadlines, discounts, admissions of liability, or other commitments you cannot make?
3. **Audience:** Does it expose internal causes, names, or confidential information?
4. **Completeness:** Are open points visibly marked instead of filled with plausible details?
5. **Tone and language:** Is the text clear, respectful, and free of unsupported judgments?

The prompt steers format and limits. A correct result it does not guarantee. "Use only these facts" and "mark gaps" make the check easier, not unnecessary.

And the time saved? Measure it in your own process. Without repeated measurement there is no defensible minute figure, from anyone.
sections.keyTakeaway: Facts, authority, audience, completeness, tone. Prompt limits make the check easier and guarantee nothing.

quiz.questionText: You have an AI assistant draft a reply to a complaint. What must you check before sending?

answerOptions.text: Whether the email is at least 300 words long
Whether the AI made specific commitments you are not authorised to make
Whether the email carries an automatic signature
Whether the draft was written in English

quiz.explanation: The assistant likes offering solutions: a discount, express delivery, a credit note. Nobody authorised them. So before you send, check the tone, every commitment and every confidential detail.

quiz.questionText: According to the course, which prompt control matters most when answering a complaint?

answerOptions.text: "Professionally" to set the basic tone
"No more than 150 words" to keep it concise
"Do not make any commitments without consulting Sales"
"Use bullet points"

quiz.explanation: Not committing without Sales is the most important limit. The assistant readily offers discounts, express deliveries, credit notes. Tone and length you can fix afterwards. A promise to the customer you cannot.

props.title: The same task, two prompts
props.bad: Write a reply to this customer email.
props.good: Context: The customer complains about a delivery that arrived two weeks late. Task: Draft a factual response using only the supplied facts. Format: email, maximum 120 words, with greeting and closing. Constraints: do not invent a cause, deadline, compensation, or corrective action; mark missing information in square brackets; do not assign blame.
props.note: Context, task, format, and constraints make the draft easier to review. They do not establish facts or approvals.

lessons.title: Summarising a meeting
lessons.subtitle: Decision or passing remark: the record knows the difference

sections.title: Option A: Copilot in Microsoft Teams
sections.content:
The licence is there. So is the button. Not enough. Before anyone records or transcribes, settle purpose, notice to participants, legal basis or consent, worker representation, retention, access rights and the concrete service.

Where the workflow is approved and the feature exists in the product, you get a draft with topics, actions and timestamps. Where the button sits depends on version and licence.

Then compare the draft against the recording, transcript or confirmed notes. Who spoke? Who owns it? Which deadline actually stands? "We could look into that" is not a decision.

The approved record goes to the participants. And they need a fixed way to get errors corrected.
sections.keyTakeaway: Recording and transcription need an approved legal and operational frame. The automatic record is a draft, read against the primary sources.

sections.title: Option B: notes and a prompt
sections.content:
No recording, only notes? An assistant can propose a structure from those, if they are approved:

"Organize the notes into confirmed decisions, tasks with explicitly named owners and deadlines, and open questions. Do not invent names, dates, or decisions. Mark missing information."

**Source notes:**
- open pipeline 1.2m, 400k prioritized
- predictive-maintenance pilot requested, 35k
- service agreement for second site, stated deadline 15.04
- some CRM records outdated
- technical data sheet required

If the draft turns that into names, new deadlines or an approved CRM cleanup, it invented them. Those points move under "open", not "decided".

And your own notes are not automatically harmless. They can carry personal, confidential or co-determination-relevant content, so only the approved workflow. Personnel, works-council and disciplinary matters follow your organization's special rules. Handwriting makes nothing lawful. Local processing neither.
sections.keyTakeaway: The draft may not add owners, deadlines or decisions. Your own notes fall under data, employment and worker-representation rules too.

quiz.questionText: Which typical error do automated AI meeting summaries make?

answerOptions.text: They delete the meeting recording after producing the summary
They sometimes confuse speakers and record passing remarks as decisions
They can summarise meetings held in English only
They send the summary to every participant automatically

quiz.explanation: Two similar voices, and the wrong name ends up on the sentence. And "it would be good to tackle that sometime" turns into a decision. Both you correct by hand.

quiz.questionText: Which rule applies to AI-supported summaries of particularly sensitive meetings?

answerOptions.text: Sales meetings about the pipeline
Weekly team stand-ups
They are allowed only in an expressly approved workflow covering purpose, legal basis, worker representation, access and retention
Meetings with more than five participants

quiz.explanation: Personnel, works council, disciplinary case: a product name does not cover it, a local installation neither. The organization approves the concrete purpose and workflow legally, technically and organizationally. Otherwise no AI processing runs.

sections.title: Four product lines, four quarters
sections.content:
Four product lines, four quarters, one table. Before anything gets calculated, settle the definitions: which column is revenue? Which unit, which currency? Net or gross? And what is an "outlier" here?

In an analysis tool approved for these data you then request a draft:

"For each product line, calculate total revenue and the percentage change from Q2 to Q4. Show the formula, reference values, and rounding. Do not infer a cause. Label a value as an outlier only if you state the method and threshold."

For the exercise you use synthetic data. Real financial data belongs only in the workflow approved for it. The enterprise tenant alone is no approval, the local installation neither.

LA-500 falls from 395 to 290. That is a drop of about -26.6 percent, and at first nothing more. Whether the value is statistically unusual depends on comparison series, method and threshold. Why it falls, four quarters will not tell you.
sections.keyTakeaway: Formula, reference values, rounding, outlier method: have them shown. A change is not a cause and not automatically a statistical outlier.

sections.title: Five checks before the report
sections.content:
**Before the report:**

1. **Check the schema:** Confirm columns, units, missing values, data types, and filters.
2. **Reproduce calculations:** Recalculate critical metrics with an independent formula or second tool. Two or three spot checks are not sufficient for every high-impact decision.
3. **Record definitions:** Document denominator, period, rounding, exclusions, and outlier method.
4. **Bound the claim:** Separate observed change, hypothesis, forecast, and supported cause.
5. **Check approval:** Confirm data class, purpose, permissions, contract, retention, region, and export functions for the exact system.

The assistant proposes formulas, sometimes interpretations. Checking is yours. You need enough subject knowledge, or someone responsible who has it. A good-sounding explanation is not evidence.
sections.keyTakeaway: Schema, calculation, definition and claim boundary all get checked. Real financial data only in the concretely approved system and workflow.

quiz.questionText: An AI assistant analyses your quarterly figures and reports a 23% fall in revenue. What should you do?

answerOptions.text: Copy the figure straight into the report, because AI calculates correctly
Recalculate two or three samples by hand and check the reference point
Discard the whole analysis and start again by hand
Repeat the prompt until the AI delivers a different figure

quiz.explanation: 23 percent, against what? A different reference point, Q1 instead of Q2, and the percentage no longer holds. Recalculate samples and check the reference point.

quiz.questionText: Why must confidential revenue figures not go into an unapproved consumer AI service?

answerOptions.text: The service has too small a character limit
For the consumer offer the organisation lacks a reviewed contract, an approval and binding data controls
Consumer offers cannot process numbers
A paid competing product would be approved automatically

quiz.explanation: The unapproved consumer offer lacks the contract and configuration frame the organisation has reviewed. Confidential financial data belongs only in an expressly approved enterprise product. And even there, data class, contract, permissions and region are checked first.

lessons.title: Writing a report
lessons.subtitle: Notes become a report. Plans stay plans.

sections.title: From bullet point to draft
sections.content:
The status report is due, you have bullet points. An assistant can order approved notes along a fixed structure. Only in the workflow approved for these data and recipients.

An instruction you can check:

"Organize the notes into status, supported risks, confirmed decisions, tasks with explicitly named owners and deadlines, and open points. Use only information from the source. Mark missing owners, dates, and evidence."

Every statement traces back to a line in the notes. "Agency quote: EUR 1,800, five working days" is a quote, not approved spending. A planned date is not a confirmed one.

An internal report can carry personal, financial or trade-secret information. "Internal" is no approval for a consumer offer. Check service and workflow.
sections.keyTakeaway: From loose bullet points the assistant makes a readable draft. Supported is only what stands in the notes.

sections.title: What you have to change
sections.content:
Four layers where a draft goes wrong:

1. **Source:** Is every number, date, person, and decision supported by the notes?
2. **Status:** Are facts, plans, assumptions, risks, and open questions clearly separated?
3. **Priority:** Was the ordering set by a responsible person rather than inferred from wording?
4. **Approval:** May the content be shared with the recipients, and has the responsible person approved the final text?

Whether it pays off, you measure: comparison cases, editing time, factual corrections, omitted risks. A percentage without a measured series is a claim, not a productivity statement.
sections.keyTakeaway: A report draft needs source checking, clear status categories, accountable prioritization and approval. Productivity is measured, not asserted.

quiz.questionText: An AI assistant builds a status report from your bullet points. What is the most important correction?

answerOptions.text: Change the font
Adjust the priorities, because the AI does not know what is urgent
Remove every number
Rewrite the whole report

quiz.explanation: The assistant does not know what is urgent. Risks and pending decisions you push to the top. Unsupported judgements and missing context stay your work.

quiz.questionText: How do you judge whether AI support improves the reporting process?

answerOptions.text: With a general vendor claim about time savings
By the length of the generated text alone
With repeated comparison cases: editing time, factual corrections and omitted risks
By assuming every generated draft has the same value

quiz.explanation: Time gain and quality depend on task, source data, tool and review effort. Repeated comparison cases give a basis that holds. A brochure figure does not.
